summary: WebinarTV used publicly discoverable Zoom registration or joining links to access sessions and publish recordings, summaries and some AI-hosted podcast versions without organisers’ or participants’ permission in documented cases. In March 2026, 404 Media examined an educators’ session on protecting students from ICE raids that was posted and made into a “Phil & Amy” AI podcast; WebinarTV removed it after the teacher objected. An April investigation found 12-step recovery and patient/caregiver support sessions on the site, including participants’ names and faces and a vetted Graves’ disease family meeting intended not to be recorded. WebinarTV’s chief executive disputed a privacy violation, describing webinars as public and claiming host contact and easy removal; the organiser said notice came after posting. A claimed corpus above 200,000 is the company’s figure, not a verified count of unauthorised sensitive sessions.

vigil_assessment.factual_basis: 404 Media directly examined a posted educators’ meeting, its AI podcast derivative, and later anonymous recovery and health-support recordings with visible identities. Kimberly Dorris of the Graves’ Disease & Thyroid Foundation said her meeting used registration screening and a waiting room, was not intended to be recorded, and appeared on WebinarTV; her original public warning now returns 410, so that proposition is reported through 404 Media rather than independently retrieved from the original post. The teacher’s meeting was removed after request; removal of other content and copies is not established. WebinarTV CEO Michael Robertson told reporters he seeks host permission and views webinars as public; the reported specific cases place posting before contact and participants’ expectations at odds with that claim. Zoom reportedly found access by public links and external screen-recording tools, not a Zoom platform breach. The American Library Association posted an institutional removal warning. NBC’s indexed investigation offers independent context but the page returned 403. The site’s greater-than-200,000 number is a self-reported corpus, not a verified harm count.
vigil_assessment.governance_interpretation: The evidence supports separate access, capture and secondary-publication mechanisms across several reported sessions. Zoom’s account attributes entry to publicly shared links and recording to external tools rather than a Zoom breach. WebinarTV’s CEO stated a public-webinar view and host contact policy, while the cases reported posting before contact and participant expectations of restricted access. Removal of the teacher’s session demonstrates one corrective action, but the record does not establish global removal or verified deletion of derivatives. Technical reachability, participant capture and later public derivative use remain separate failures grounded in inspected sessions and attributed organizer testimony. Removal of one session is bounded recovery; the company’s corpus number is not an unauthorized-session count. Bias-correction permissions, model-development security and model-agent admission concern different objects from the supported operational capture/publication mechanism. The privacy and autonomy outcome is Not aligned for the inspected sessions. Removal of the teacher’s session is Aligned as a limited corrective action. The inspected recordings disclosed contributions from private support and health meetings, including visible identities. The identified screened meeting was not intended to be recorded. The documented publication before permission crossed that confidentiality boundary; the site’s claimed overall corpus is not treated as a count of unauthorised disclosures.
vigil_assessment.significance_to_cam: The later sensitive-session reporting shows why “webinar” and a discoverable link are poor proxies for consent. The same content crossed entry, participant-capture and publication/derivative-purpose boundaries; each needs separate authority. Actual exposed names and faces in recovery and health contexts support a more serious realised privacy outcome than the site’s self-reported corpus number.

source_clause_analysis.purpose: Primary and first-hand reporting reconstructed as material external action, risk/control effect and response episodes; provider assertions and observation scope are distinguished rather than mechanically asserted as independently proven.

clauses.source_paraphrase: In March and April 2026 reporting, WebinarTV used publicly discoverable Zoom webinar/join links to enter sessions that some organisers and attendees understood to be private or limited to invitees. Zoom indicated the links had been shared publicly. Discoverability supplied a technically usable path, but the affected hosts contested whether that conferred permission to republish attendees' contributions.
clauses.recovered_invariant_interpretation: A technically reachable joining link establishes a route of access, not authority to enter a session whose intended audience and access conditions are narrower.

taxonomy_relationships.rationale: The reported use of discoverable links to enter sessions treated technical reachability as sufficient authority despite the stated restricted purpose and audience.

clauses.source_paraphrase: WebinarTV made recordings of sessions it joined, including an educators' meeting and later documented support-group and health-related sessions. 404 Media identified recordings showing participant names and faces, including in settings where anonymity or privacy was expected. This is an observed recording/distribution mechanism; it does not independently establish that every one of the site's claimed 200,000 webinars was non-consensual.
clauses.recovered_invariant_interpretation: A host’s ability to organise or link a meeting does not itself authorise covert recording and processing of every participant’s identifiable contribution.

taxonomy_relationships.rationale: Reporting and directly inspected posted sessions establish multi-party participant contributions being recorded without separately established participant authority, including sensitive support contexts.
The investigator inspected posted support-group recordings showing names and faces. The identified private health meeting had screened attendance and was not intended for recording.

clauses.source_paraphrase: The service published recordings and, in the educators' case, produced an AI-hosted podcast-style derivative before receiving the affected teacher's permission. In later reporting the operator argued the sessions were public webinars, said hosts were contacted about promotion and pointed to a removal process. The journalists' documented order of posting and requests challenged the claim that publication always followed approval.
clauses.recovered_invariant_interpretation: Access for attendance or capture does not authorise public archival, promotion or derivative media use; publication authority must be established for the affected session and audience.

taxonomy_relationships.rationale: The reports place public posting and AI-podcast adaptation before contact with the educator, and identify sensitive recordings posted without independent publication authority.
Recordings and the educator’s AI derivative were published before permission was obtained. Discoverable join links did not authorise disclosure of private participant contributions.

clauses.source_paraphrase: After the affected educator objected in March, WebinarTV removed that identified educators' recording. Later April reporting found other recorded support/recovery sessions still posted; the single removal did not establish eradication of all copies or a general preventive restriction.
clauses.recovered_invariant_interpretation: A targeted removal can contain a known publication instance, but recovery should be scoped and verified across derivative and remaining copies before treating the exposure as closed.

harm_impact_assessment.coverage_note: All twelve dimensions reviewed. Directly inspected identifiable recovery and health-support recordings support retained S4 privacy impact. Public links do not establish participant consent. Removal of one teacher’s publication does not restore every recording, derivative or copy. The company’s 200,000-webinar claim is not a verified sensitive-victim count. Relational-role and heightened personal-protection recognition and exclusions independently tested.
